testFuzz_AdjustmentsStayWithinTheImmutab.details: They are additive and non-negative: MIN is unreachable from above, MAX is clamped.

test_BlueSupplyRateIsRealAndSane().details: The floor is worth nothing if the number behind it is a stub. This measures it on the      fork, against the same USDC/WETH market the idle sleeve actually sits in.

test_FloorAboveTheHardMaxStopsTheQuote().details: The alternative would be to clamp at MAX_RATE_BPS and keep buying below the floor —      exactly the value destruction the floor forbids. Refusing to quote is the only honest      answer. Blue paying 35% does not happen on the fork, hence the mock.

test_PolicyWithoutVaultRefusesToQuote().details: Failing closed matters here: an unskewed, unfloored quote is precisely the static bid      this whole mechanism replaces, and a half-finished deployment must not produce one.

test_RatificationGasWithTheDynamicPolicy.details: `isRatified` now reads Blue's rate model on top of the vault's own book. The bound is      deliberately loose — it is an alarm for a change that made ratification expensive, not      a performance target. What would be unacceptable is a seller giving up on the take.

test_SkewMovesTheBidAsTheBookFills().details: This is the whole point of the skew. The cap is still there and still binds, but the      approach to it is now priced: each lot is bought a little cheaper than the last, so      concentration is paid for by the seller who causes it rather than worn by depositors.

test_SkewSaturatesWhenHeldExceedsTheCap(.details: Reachable in one move: the owner lowers `maxUnits` under a book already built.

test_StaleBidIsRefusedOnceTheSkewHasMove.details: The offer sitting in the Mempool is a struct with a fixed tick; nothing cancels it. What      protects the vault is that `isRatified` re-reads the policy at the instant of the take,      and the policy has moved. Without the skew this could only happen when the owner changed      the rate; with it, the vault's own fills disarm its stale offers.

test_VolSpreadPricesCollateralRisk().details: The spread is flat and configured, not inferred — but it is applied by the same      on-chain path as the rest, so the bot cannot quote around it.

failed().notice: Returns true if any test assertion has failed.

targetSenders().notice: Returns sender allowlist configured via `targetSender` (empty means no sender allowlist).

testFuzz_AdjustmentsStayWithinTheImmutab.notice: The adjustments can never breach the immutable bounds.

test_BlueSupplyRateIsRealAndSane().notice: The vault reads a real, non-zero supply rate from the live Blue market.

test_EnabledMarketNeedsANonZeroCap().notice: An enabled market with no cap cannot be priced, so it cannot be configured.

test_FloorAboveTheHardMaxStopsTheQuote().notice: When Blue out-earns anything Plumb may legitimately bid, Plumb stops quoting.

test_FloorDoesNotTouchARateAlreadyAboveI.notice: Above the floor, the floor is inert — it is a floor, not a peg.

test_FloorLiftsARateThatWouldDestroyValu.notice: Below the floor, Plumb demands the floor — it never buys under its own idle yield.

test_OnlyOwnerSetsVaultAndMargin().notice: Only the owner moves the policy's own wiring.
